title: Class Dashboard Load Estimator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Analytics
LRS-Lite
Dashboards
description: Calculate how much a teacher's browser must download to build an LRS-Lite class dashboard, estimate the load-time band, and decide when the design's rollup function is needed.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the download size and load-time band for a teacher dashboard at a given roster size and decide whether the design's rollup function is needed.
prerequisites: Browser-side dashboards and object storage sync (Chapter 23)

accessibility.notes: Native range inputs; canvas aria-label; text panel is an aria-live region.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Calculator with thresholds and an explicit decision message
keyQuestions: How many files and megabytes does the teacher download?
At what roster size should the rollup function be used?
commonMisconceptions: That a larger summary size changes the rollup threshold
That the time band is a measurement
assessmentOpportunities: Recommend enabling the rollup for a described school

equations: load band (s) = students * [5, 20] ms + total MB / [10, 2.5] MB/s (illustrative)
assumptions: 11 KB per summary and the 100-student threshold are design estimates
Load band calibrated to the design statement that 150 students load in about 1-4 s
limitations: The load-time band and rollup size are illustrative, not measured
